title: Retrieve, Match, Escalate: Accurate and Scalable Product Linking with VLM-Distilled Cross-Encoders and Agentic VLMs

visual_explainer.question: When should a production cascade pay for an agentic multimodal web-search stage?
visual_explainer.takeaway: A cheap matcher resolves high-confidence traffic and escalates only the ambiguous tail to a VLM that can inspect images and search the web; selective escalation, not universal agent use, is the economic control point.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Cheap-stage-only production coverage, trained human review on the hard tail, and open versus closed agentic VLM stacks at equal precision.

analysis.tldr: A production product-linking cascade spends expensive multimodal web-search reasoning only on the ambiguous tail. The evidence supports confidence-gated escalation as a cost/coverage control surface, but it does not isolate web search from the VLM, images, prompts, and other Stage-3 changes.
analysis.problem: Billions of merchant records must be linked against large catalogs at high precision, while using a frontier multimodal agent on every candidate pair would be prohibitively expensive.
analysis.core_idea: Retrieve candidates, let a distilled cross-encoder auto-resolve confident pairs, reject low-confidence pairs, and escalate only the medium-confidence residual to an agentic VLM with image inspection and web search.
analysis.agent_loop: multimodal retrieval → cheap cross-encoder score → accept/reject or escalate → agentic VLM inspects record and image → optional web search → enough-evidence decision → final link judgment
analysis.retrieval_design: Retrieval coverage is measured separately from downstream matching; the main adaptive retrieval decision is whether the hard tail receives external web evidence at all.
compared_to: cheap-stage-only production linking at the same operating precision bar
trained human operators on the hardest medium-confidence cases
open-weight versus closed frontier VLM hard-tail agents at equal 98% precision
analysis.evidence: On roughly two million production records, the previous-generation cheap stage links 68.1% at the operating precision bar and hard-tail escalation raises coverage to 77.1%. On a separate equal-precision audit, the open-weight agent reaches 88% recall versus 92% for the closed stack at about one-seventh the per-pair cost; on hardest medium cases a closed VLM reaches 96.7% accuracy versus 83.0% for trained operators.
analysis.why_it_matters: It supplies production evidence that the dominant systems decision may be selective escalation into expensive evidence acquisition rather than making every query maximally agentic.
limitations: The 68.1% to 77.1% production uplift uses a previous-generation cheap linker, so it is a property of the escalated hard tail rather than a matched evaluation of the final Stage-2 model.
There is no matched same-VLM no-web-search control, so the Stage-3 gain cannot be attributed specifically to external search.
Retrieval recall remains an upstream ceiling; downstream reasoning cannot repair a missing candidate.
Per-pair agent costs and coverage are reported, but a fully matched end-to-end latency/token accounting across all cascade variants is incomplete.
